A public library organizes books, magazines, maps, and other reference materials so visitors can find reliable information. A catalogue describes each item and records where it belongs. Librarians help readers choose sources, compare different accounts, and locate relevant chapters. Quiet study areas give people space to concentrate, while meeting rooms allow small groups to discuss projects. A lending desk records which books have been borrowed and when they are due back. Some collections include local newspapers and historical photographs that preserve details about a community. Digital catalogues can be searched by author, title, subject, or publication date. Visitors may consult several sources before forming a conclusion. A useful reference service explains where an answer came from and distinguishes established facts from uncertain interpretations. Building maintenance, clear signs, comfortable seating, and accessible entrances also matter because they make the collection easier to use. Public events may include reading groups, exhibitions, and talks. These activities serve different needs, but all rely on careful organization and clear communication. This passage is background information about a library. The question below is a separate general knowledge question.

What is the capital city of France? Reply with exactly the city name, without punctuation or explanation.
